newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CND to discuss railway and ports Sept 24.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CND to discuss railway and ports Sept 24.

text.p: Brazil's National Privatization Council (CND) will set the dates for the auction of two more sections of the federal railway network at its next meeting September 24, said Planning Minister Antonio Kandir.

Kandir, who was attending Friday's privatization auction in Rio of the southeast section of the federal railway, said the CND would set dates for the auctions of the Teresa Cristina and the southern section of the federal railway September 24. He said the auctions would take place in November and December, respectively.

The Teresa Cristina section with a minimum price of 13.6 million reais ($13.6 million) is located in Santa Catarina state and the southern section with a minimum price of 158 million reais ($158 million) links Rio Grande do Sul, Parana and Santa Catarina states.
He said the CND meeting would focus otherwise on the privatization of Brazil's ports.
"I am very satisfied to see the privatization program moving full steam ahead," Kandir said. "In our battle to reduce the cost of doing business in Brazil we are now obsessed with the port sector."

Brazilian Transport Minister Alcides Saldanha said the ports of Itajai and Laguna in Santa Catarina state, Cabedelo in Paraiba state and Porto Velho in Rondonia state were first in line to be privatized followed by Manaus, Recife and Maceio. Concessions to operate all seven ports are to be sold at auction still this year.
Brazil's main ports of Santos, Rio de Janeiro, Sepetiba and Paranagua will be privatized in 1997, Saldanha added.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
